name: France-Merrick Foundation Environment Grants
summary: One-time capital, equipment and technology grants from a Maryland foundation for nonprofits preserving and restoring Maryland waters, habitats and natural areas. Requests over USD 50,000 follow set letter-of-inquiry dates.
reporting: Final report, generally due one year after the final payment.

steps: Letter of Inquiry (rolling; over $50,000 by the closing date)

eligibility.rule: Holds 501(c)(3) status or uses a 501(c)(3) fiscal agent in good standing
Has at least three board officers: president, secretary and treasurer
Has at least 51% unrelated voting board members
Applies for a one-time project with defined beginnings and endings
Has financial stability to sustain the project
Not for individuals, special events, debt or deficits, political activities or general operating costs
No France-Merrick grant final payment in the last two years

calls.label: Letters of inquiry (rolling)

status.quote: We accept LOIs on a rolling basis and encourage organizations to send them anytime.

calls.note: Requests over $50,000 wait for set LOI closing dates

applicant_types.quote: Legal organization name, mailing address and 501(c)(3) Tax ID number of the organization/fiscal sponsor

geography.quote: supporting organizations that are involved in preserving and protecting the waters and natural areas in the State of Maryland

access.quote: the first step for an organization interested in applying for a grant is to send the Foundation a 1-3 page Letter of Inquiry (LOI)

window.quote: We accept LOIs on a rolling basis and encourage organizations to send them anytime.

reporting.quote: Final reports are generally due one year after the final payment date.

effort.quote: We accept LOIs on a rolling basis and encourage organizations to send them anytime.
One month after decision is made on LOI
Once received, each proposal is assigned to a staff member, who conducts a thorough review including follow-up questions and a site visit.

eligibility.quote: Applicants must be a non-profit organization holding 501(c)(3) status under the Internal Revenue Code or have a 501(c)(3) fiscal agent in good standing.
Per Maryland law, the non-profit must have at least three officers on its Board of Directors: president, secretary, and treasurer.
Per U.S. law, the Board of Directors must have at least 51% "unrelated" voting board members, who are not related by family or through business partnerships.
The Foundation funds one-time projects with defined beginnings and endings.
Applicants must have the financial stability to sustain the project for which funding is sought.
Individuals Special events or advertising space in programs Deficit financing/debt reduction Political activities General operating/annual giving
Per Foundation policy, new funding requests may only be submitted after completing a two-year waiting period from the final payment date of a previous grant.

after_award.quote: Final reports are generally due one year after the final payment date.
